Fiasco

/fee-AH-sko/ — rhymes with tobacco · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A fiasco is a complete and often embarrassing failure.

The outdoor wedding became a fiasco when the tent collapsed into the cake.

Worked Example

The school's first robotics competition turned into a fiasco when half the teams' robots malfunctioned, the scoreboard broke, and the award ceremony was cancelled.

Fiasco suggests not just any failure, but a total, spectacular, and often humiliating collapse. Words like 'failure' or 'mistake' don't capture the full scale and embarrassment baked into fiasco.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

failure: an attempt that does not succeed

disaster: informally, anything that goes badly wrong

debacle: a sudden, humiliating collapse of plans

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

success: an outcome that goes as planned

triumph: a great and celebrated victory

Where it sits · how total and embarrassing the collapse — slip → failure → disaster → fiasco

slip vs. fiasco: A slip is far weaker than a fiasco: a slip is one small mistake, while a fiasco is a plan collapsing completely — and embarrassingly — from start to finish.

failure vs. fiasco: Failure is weaker than fiasco — a failure simply doesn't succeed, but a fiasco fails so totally and so publicly that it becomes humiliating.

disaster vs. fiasco: Disaster, in its casual everyday sense, is strong, but fiasco tops it on this scale: a disaster went very badly, while a fiasco collapsed so completely that everyone watching cringed.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fiasco

Root — fiasco: bottle (from Late Latin flasco) (Italian)

Put it together

Put it together: Fiasco is simply the Italian word for 'bottle,' from Late Latin flasco. In Italian theater slang, far fiasco — 'to make a bottle' — meant to fail a performance completely; no one is sure why the bottle image stuck, but the meaning did: a total, embarrassing failure.

Use the root in a new word: flask

Use the root in a new word: flask: A flask is a small bottle, and it shares fiasco's root, Late Latin flasco, 'bottle' — in Italian, 'making a bottle' (far fiasco) became slang for failing completely and embarrassingly.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Fiasco names a complete, spectacular failure, often with an embarrassing or public element. For a smaller setback or simple unsuccessful attempt, choose 'failure' or 'mishap' instead.
